patent: CBN Nano Technologies patent (inventors Ryley III, Jobes, MacArthur, Semprebon), provisionals filed 2020-09-25, PCT filed 2021-09-22, issued 2023-08-08. A catalogue of mechanical logic gates in which input positions decide whether the displacement of a driven (clock) element reaches an output. Schemes run from aligned knob rows and deflected flexible rods through moved guides, constrained hinges, link-and-pivot axis alignment, shaped plates coupled by non-contact forces and rotary tabs, then adder, flip-flop and grid-memory compositions. The text gives scales from macroscopic models to mechanosynthesized parts. Its molecular-scale figures are stated as modeling or expectation: molecular modeling for a 30 nm cube gate, molecular dynamics for actuation below 100 pN or 10 pN. The document reports no fabricated or tested device. It names US 10,481,866 and related filings as earlier designs for reduced energy consumption, and states no energy figure of its own.

glossary.def: Here, part 1534: a bar pinned to two inputs that positions a connector link by their combined positions (FIG. 15C). Hinge 510 in FIG. 5 plays a similar role under a different name. "Lock-and-balance" in col. 23 names a scheme the patent only refers to, in US 10,481,866 and related filings.
The word does not appear in this description. Compliance comes from elements it calls resiliently flexible (606), flexible (706, 810, 1042), and from hinges and pivots.

Computing that does not erase information, so Landauer's bound of kT ln 2 per erased bit need not apply. The word appears here only in cited titles on the reference pages, such as Merkle's "Two Types of Mechanical Reversible Logic". The description says only "reduced energy consumption", and of the earlier filings.

Logic driven slowly enough that dissipation falls as operation slows, with energy recovered from the drive. The word does not appear in this description, which claims no such behavior for these gates.
The part the mechanism tries to move, often the mechanical clock. The text counts it as an optional extra input. Its motion reaches an output only if inputs provide a path.
Mechanical displacement applied in phases, Clk1, Clk2, Clk3. Generators are out of scope here; the text refers to US 10,683,924 and PCT/US2020/031645.
Single rail: one line per signal, moved or not moved. Dual rail: a separate line per value (A=0, A=1). FIGS. 1A-3C are dual rail at the output; FIG. 3D is single rail.
Block on an input that pushes its neighbor. A complete row of knobs is the motion path; a gap breaks it.
The claim terms: the two configurations of the control structure, in which the driven element's motion is absorbed without output motion, or transmitted to the output.
Mechanical pass gate: one input decides whether motion passes from driven element to output. Same name as the CMOS (complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor) pass device; no electrical meaning here.
Two opposed transmission gates on one input and one driven element: motion goes to one of two outputs.
NOR or NAND: any Boolean function can be built from it alone.
Half adder: sum and carry of two bits. Full adder: same with a carry-in.
One-bit store that takes its data input when clocked. Here two latches of FIG. 17A in a loop with sequenced locks.
Here: holds the value when input and clock are released, because the lock plate blocks the copy pin.

Coupling without touching surfaces: magnetic, electrostatic or van der Waals. A part held by NCF resists leaving the plate at an edge, and that resistance acts as a detent. Pins may also be in contact, as the text allows.
Short-range attraction between neutral atoms or surfaces, dominant at nanometer gaps. It scales with overlap area, which is why edges act as barriers and why tracks 512 keep overlap constant.
The patent's spelling of complementary: an output carrying the opposite value.
Carbon nanotube with chiral indices (n, 0), zigzag type. 10-0, 18-0 and 9-0 in col. 24 set diameter and how sections nest or bond. 18-0 sleeves fit around 10-0 rods.
Diamondoid: diamond-like sp3 carbon structures. Lonsdaleite: hexagonal polymorph of diamond, used here as the anchor surface matched by 9-0 tubes.
Linear carbon chain with alternating single and triple bonds, proposed in col. 12 for flexible parts.
Building a structure atom by atom using mechanically positioned tips. The text names patents for it; it reports no use of it for these gates.
Micro- and nanoelectromechanical systems: machines made with lithographic fabrication. The text lists these as alternative routes to fabricate these mechanisms.
Drexler's 1992 nanotechnology design: sliding rods block one another. The background cites it as prior context.
Output displacement larger than driven displacement, from a lever ratio on the plate (FIG. 14).
